messages:
Alex K: hey, ran an nsys trace on the latest runtime image and a bunch of kernels have no symbol/line info — just hex offsets and "<unknown>" entries. super noisy when trying to map hotspots.
Maria S: ugh. did we switch to a multistage build that strips debug info? any recent changes to nvcc flags in the CI image? :thinking_face:
Alex K: build-bot shows the image was rebuilt last night. build logs include `strip --strip-all` in the final stage. suspect that's the culprit for host-side symbolization.
build-bot: CI: image-redwood/runtime:nightly built by pipeline #4821, final stage applied `strip` step (see /ci/logs/4821).
Devon R: also check NVTX/CUPTI availability inside container. If nsight can't load CUPTI or version mismatches it sometimes fails to resolve kernel names. did you see any CUPTI warnings in nsys output?
Alex K: yes there was a CUPTI warning: "CUPTI: CUPTI library not found or version mismatch; symbolization may be incomplete."
Maria S: steps to debug (short):
- ensure user binary and cuda lib symbols are present (no strip)
- compile kernels with nvcc flags `-g -lineinfo` (device line mappings)
- run nsys from host or include CUPTI in container and match toolkit version
Devon R: exact examples we used:
```
# compile example
nvcc -O3 -g -lineinfo -Xcompiler "-fno-omit-frame-pointer" -arch=sm_80 -o my_kernel.so my_kernel.cu
# DO NOT run strip on the final shared object
```
Jin (perf): quick note: `-g` vs `-G` — `-G` enables device-side debugging and slows kernels massively; we usually use `-g -lineinfo` for symbolization without slowdowns.
Alex K: thanks. tried a rebuild locally with `-g -lineinfo` and skipped strip. trace improved but still ~30% of kernel launches show as addresses with no source line. sample from nsys timeline: `kernel: 0x7f1ae2c8 <unknown> (kernel_launch)`
Devon R: that pattern usually means CUPTI couldn't match the binary ID to the running kernel. two common causes: (1) the runtime in container uses a different CUDA toolkit (libcupti) than host nsys, (2) the binary was JITed or uses fatbin with no embedded lineinfo.
Maria S: try this docker run variant to ensure CUPTI/toolkit visibility:
```
docker run --gpus all --rm -it \ 
  -v /usr/local/cuda:/usr/local/cuda:ro \ 
  -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH \ 
  runtime-image:dev ./run_inference
```
Alex K: ran that. nsys output improved but still some kernels unresolved. also noticed container was built against CUDA 11.8 while host driver toolkit is 12.x — could that break symbolization?
Devon R: yes, CUPTI lib and the driver toolchain must be compatible. nsight uses CUPTI to query kernel debug info mapping; mismatched major versions can lead to partial info. try running nsys from inside the same container that has the matching toolkit (install nsight-cli in the container) OR run the container with host's /usr/local/cuda bind-mounted so CUPTI and libcuda are consistent.
Jin (perf): another subtle one — LTO / linker garbage collection can remove or fold symbols. check if the final link used `-Wl,--gc-sections` or link-time-optimization flags. if so, disable for builds you intend to profile.
Alex K: good catch. our release Dockerfile applies LTO and a final `strip`. going to make a profiling variant without those steps.
Maria S: when you re-run nsys, use a verbose capture and save the report:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_prof --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --cuda-memory-usage true ./run_inference
nsys stats trace_prof.qdrep
```
look for `cuptiActivityKindKernel` entries and cross-check `correlationId` -> kernel name mapping.
Devon R: if line numbers still missing, collect CUPTI logs: set env `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_LOG=./cup​ti.log` (some installs support this) and capture stderr from nsight to see mapping warnings.
Alex K: did a run with profiling image (no strip, -g -lineinfo, CUPTI mounted). results: majority symbolized, but some kernels (short 1-2ms transients) still show up as `unknown`. output excerpt: 
```
[Kernel] start 0.120s dur 0.0012s id 3452 -> name: <unknown> addr 0x7f8af2c0
[Kernel] start 0.121s dur 0.045s id 3453 -> name: matmul_tiled_kernel (matched)
```
Jin (perf): short-lived kernels can be optimized away or inlined into other launches. Also check whether we have runtime kernel fusion in the driver or our launcher is creating many tiny kernels. If the kernel is launched from JIT code (e.g., via cubin loaded at runtime) symbolization is trickier.
Maria S: next actions:
- Alex: upload one sample qdrep + full .qdump (or the sys trace) to the perf bucket
- Build-team: create a `profiling` docker flavor (no strip, no LTO, -g -lineinfo) in CI
- Infra: ensure nightly images keep a non-stripped artifact for debugging
Alex K: uploading trace_prof.qdrep to gs://redwood-perf/traces/1719854321/ now. link: https://storage.redwood.internal/perf/traces/1719854321/trace_prof.qdrep
Devon R: I'll try to reproduce locally with same image and run `strings`/`objdump -t` on the .so to confirm symbols present. if they are and nsight still can't match, we escalate to NVIDIA (CUPTI).
Alex K: thanks all — feel like we have a clear path. will follow up after we test profiling image and confirm CUPTI/toolkit alignment. :thumbsup:
